2610.32347.title: Entangled logical qubits on a superconducting quantum processor
2610.32347.abstract: We demonstrate high-fidelity logical qubit operations using \texttt{ibm\_phoenix}, a square-lattice array of 120 coupled superconducting qubits that are capable of fast reset. Using strategies to exclude underperforming components together with noise informed decoding, we routinely produce surface codes at distance-3 and distance-5 with logical error per round below 1\%. We demonstrate entanglement between two logical qubits, where logical Bell-state fidelities above 93\% are observed for entanglement created via lattice surgery. With three logical qubits and lattice surgery, we perform logical teleportation of a range of states and gates, observing fidelities in the range 78\% - 93\%. Using reset to reduce qubit leakage, we show that repeated rounds of stabilizer measurements continue to exhibit improvements in a stability experiment up to $\sim 2\cdot 10^{-7}$ over 170 measurement rounds.
2610.32347.why: IBM's 120-qubit ibm_phoenix runs distance-5 surface codes below 1% per round, entangles logical qubits, and teleports logical states via lattice surgery.

eli5.plain: IBM made error-protected 'logical' qubits on a 120-qubit chip, entangled two of them and teleported quantum states between them.
eli5.how: Surface codes at distance 3 and 5 spread each logical qubit over many physical qubits; lattice surgery, merging and splitting code patches, creates logical Bell pairs (above 93%) and teleportation (78–93%).
eli5.matters: Operations between logical qubits, not just memory, are the next milestone after below-threshold storage, and IBM is now doing them on a square lattice with fast reset.
eli5.caveat: Underperforming components are excluded by hand and decoding is noise-informed, so how this scales without hand-picking is not shown.

2610.29986.title: Meter-scale quantum interconnects between large quantum processors
2610.29986.abstract: Modular quantum architecture requires long-distance quantum interconnects to stitch together individual processor modules. Such interconnects, long-distance couplers or L-couplers, must support coherent quantum operation over meter-scale distances and scale to multiple connections between any two modules. Here we demonstrate four L-couplers operating between two 120-qubit IBM Nighthawk R1 superconducting qubit processors. Each L-coupler joins two Nighthawk lattice qubits through two frequency-tunable L-qubits, two RF-SQUID based "i2m" couplers, and 80 cm of superconducting aluminum coax. Each cable installs perpendicular to the processor surface, to enable denser connections, and is joined to the chip by an indium-to-indium room temperature pressure bond made after both modules were mounted. L-coupler modes near 5 GHz, with internal quality factors of 0.86 to 1.09e6, carry relay-based state transfer at a mean network benchmarking fidelity of 99.00%, with a best link of 99.29 +/- 0.07%. We then realize distant CZ gates between lattice qubits in separate modules at a mean fidelity of 94.75%, with a best link of 96.42 +/- 0.28%, and use them to generate entangled states across the two processors, including a demonstration of simultaneous Bell pair generation using two adjacent L-couplers. These four high-fidelity L-couplers establish a practical path to scalable quantum interconnects for modular quantum computing.
2610.29986.why: Four 80 cm coax links coherently couple two 120-qubit IBM processors, a working meter-scale microwave interconnect between modules.

eli5.plain: IBM wired two separate quantum chips together with superconducting cables almost a meter long and showed qubits on different chips can still talk quantum-mechanically.
eli5.how: Each link runs from a lattice qubit through a tunable 'L-qubit' and a SQUID-based coupler into 80 cm of aluminium coax, which carries the microwave excitation between modules; cables plug in vertically to save chip area.
eli5.matters: This is state transfer between remote nodes over a real microwave line, the same physics as microwave quantum networks, now running between production-scale processors.
eli5.caveat: The abstract does not give transfer fidelities or loss per link here, and four links between two chips is still far from a dense multi-module fabric.

2610.32319.title: Finite Nonsignalling Resources Suffice to Simulate Entangled Qubits
2610.32319.abstract: A longstanding question in Bell nonlocality is whether finite-alphabet nonsignalling resources can reproduce the continuum of measurement correlations of partially entangled qubits. Here we resolve this problem by showing that every fixed pure two-qubit state admits an exact simulation of all local projective-measurement statistics using shared randomness and finitely many Popescu-Rohrlich (PR) boxes, without communication or postselection. The boxes operate in parallel, with a worst-case bound independent of the measurement settings: at most $128\cot^4θ$ calls for the Schmidt state $\cosθ|00\rangle+\sinθ|11\rangle$, $0<θ<π/4$. The key is an exact finite-selection method that reduces input-dependent continuous sampling to a choice from a fixed-length shared random list, implemented through a finite PR-box network. The construction extends to arbitrary mixed two-qubit states and local binary-outcome POVMs. This reveals a fundamental separation between the continuity of quantum measurement correlations and the alphabet size of the resources needed to simulate them, shedding light on the resource-theoretic structure of Bell nonlocality.
2610.32319.why: Every pure two-qubit state's projective statistics are exactly simulated with finitely many PR boxes, at most 128·cot⁴θ calls.

eli5.plain: They prove that the infinitely many possible measurement correlations of an entangled qubit pair can be faked exactly with a finite number of idealised nonlocal boxes and shared randomness.
eli5.how: A finite-selection trick turns choosing from a continuous family of measurement settings into picking from a fixed random list, which a network of PR boxes can implement with no communication.
eli5.matters: It sharpens how much nonlocality an entangled qubit pair carries: continuous correlations do not need a continuous resource, which changes how one should count 'quantum' in a Bell experiment.
eli5.caveat: The bound blows up as the state approaches product (θ→0), and PR boxes are hypothetical; this is a resource statement, not a physical model.

2610.27834.title: Controlled-Z Gates via Floquet Coupling to Two Auxiliary States in Transmon Circuits
2610.27834.abstract: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for quantum information processing. In transmon circuits, higher excited states provide additional pathways for engineering interactions within the computational subspace. Here we demonstrate controlled-Z (CZ) gates that exploit two noncomputational states, $\ket{02}$ and $\ket{20}$, through selective Floquet coupling. The nontrivial parametric modulation can activate both auxiliary transitions from $\ket{11}$ while suppressing the leading exchange between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$. Based on this approach, we develop two gate protocols: a nonadiabatic round trip through a bright auxiliary superposition and adiabatic evolution along a zero-energy dark state, both achieving average gate fidelities above $99.99\%$ in numerical simulations. Control of the modulation phase further extends the bright-state protocol to conventional and unconventional geometric CZ gates. Effective-model simulations show that unconventional control improves tolerance to residual $ZZ$ coupling and static qubit-frequency offsets relative to conventional control over the parameter ranges examined. Simulations including neighboring spectator qubits show that the original nonadiabatic bright-state and adiabatic dark-state CZ protocols retain high gate fidelities. This framework offers new routes toward the experimental realization of CZ gates and their geometric implementations.
2610.27834.why: Floquet-couples |11⟩ to both |02⟩ and |20⟩ while suppressing |01⟩–|10⟩ exchange, giving two new CZ gate protocols on transmons.

eli5.plain: A new way to make the standard two-qubit gate on transmons, borrowing two higher energy levels instead of one.
eli5.how: A parametric drive opens transitions from the both-excited state to two auxiliary states at once, while cancelling the swap between singly excited states; the round trip imprints the needed phase.
eli5.matters: More pathways means more freedom to trade speed against leakage and crosstalk, which is where CZ gates still lose fidelity.
eli5.caveat: Fidelities are not given in the abstract, so whether this beats standard flux-pulsed CZ is unclear.

2610.31632.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
2610.31632.abstract: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.
2610.31632.why: No-go theorem: a unique pre-existing 'true value' in quantum estimation is incompatible with complete states plus probe–system entanglement.

eli5.plain: They prove that quantum metrology cannot mean 'finding out a value that was already there' unless you accept hidden variables or new physics that stops entanglement.
eli5.how: They generalise estimation to quantities that fluctuate quantum-mechanically, list the assumptions behind 'true value' talk, and show these clash with state completeness and generic probe–system entanglement.
eli5.matters: It puts the measurement problem inside ordinary parameter estimation, the language used for every qubit-frequency or photon-number estimate; realism about measured values has a price.
eli5.caveat: The theorem hinges on how 'true value' is formalised; a reader who treats parameters as classical settings, not quantum variables, escapes it.

2610.24212.title: Optimal robust single-qubit gates in superconducting quantum processors
2610.24212.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity quantum gates that are resilient to control errors and device imperfections. Here, we develop energy-optimal control pulses for single-qubit gates that are simultaneously robust against frequency detuning and waveform inhomogeneities while also suppressing leakage outside the computational subspace. Combining the optimized pulse envelopes with an adaptive control scheme, we experimentally demonstrate optimal robust gates on a superconducting quantum processor. For a gate duration of 90ns, we achieve fidelities above 99.9% for the X gate and 99.6% for Hadamard-type gates. For the X gate, we maintain fidelities above 99.5% for simultaneous drive-amplitude variations up to 20% and qubit detuning up to 4 MHz. This robustness outperforms that of conventional Gaussian pulses by an order of magnitude, without much difference in peak gate fidelity. These results establish a route towards robust single-qubit control in large-scale quantum processors, advancing the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing.
2610.24212.why: Energy-optimal robust single-qubit pulses keep X-gate fidelity above 99.5% under detuning and waveform errors, with leakage suppressed, on hardware.

eli5.plain: They designed microwave pulses for single-qubit gates that keep working even when the qubit frequency or pulse shape drifts.
eli5.how: Optimal control finds pulse envelopes that cancel first-order sensitivity to detuning and amplitude errors and avoid exciting the third level; an adaptive loop tunes them on the device.
eli5.matters: Robust gates reduce how often a large processor has to be recalibrated.
eli5.caveat: 90 ns gates are slow compared with typical 20–40 ns single-qubit gates, and 99.9% is not a record.

2610.27137.title: Active isolation of transmon readout with a tunable inductive bridge
2610.27137.abstract: Scalable superconducting quantum computation requires fast, high-fidelity readout. Currently, this is assisted through cryogenic amplification of the readout signal. In traditional dispersive readout schemes, the amplifiers that are used to provide high signal-to-noise ratio also generate thermal noise that can decohere the qubits, demanding additional ferrite-based isolators to suppress this noise. Here, we integrate a chip-scale microwave switch, the tunable inductive bridge, into the readout chain of a fixed-frequency transmon. Flux-pulsing the switch, such that it transmits only during the readout, did not make a discernable difference to qubit coherence, residual excited-state population, or readout fidelity metrics. By injecting broadband noise that mimics amplifier thermal photons, we show that the switch suppresses the resulting qubit dephasing by more than $30$~dB, consistent with its independently measured on-off ratio, establishing it as a potential chip-based integrated replacement for readout-chain isolators.
2610.27137.why: An on-chip flux-pulsed inductive-bridge switch isolates a transmon from amplifier noise without hurting coherence, a step toward removing ferrite isolators.

eli5.plain: They put a fast on-chip microwave switch in the readout line that only opens during measurement, to block noise flowing back from the amplifier.
eli5.how: A tunable inductive bridge is flux-pulsed to transmit only while reading out; the rest of the time it reflects amplifier back-action away from the qubit.
eli5.matters: Bulky magnetic isolators are one of the main obstacles to scaling readout wiring; a chip switch could replace them.
eli5.caveat: Coherence and residual population were merely not worse; it is a single fixed-frequency transmon, not a multiplexed chain.

2610.27854.title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
2610.27854.abstract: Concatenation of quantum repeater nodes has been proposed as a means to distribute entanglement efficiently across future long-distance networks. Here, we demonstrate a trapped-ion repeater node that establishes photonic entanglement over a 17 km fiber traversing a city, moving beyond laboratory-only prototypes. The node comprises two atomic ions coupled to an optical cavity. First, a detailed characterization is performed of the long fiber channel and of ion-photon entanglement distributed across it. Next, a repeater-node protocol is implemented, achieving entanglement between a local photon and a remote photon with a Bell-state fidelity of $81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\%$. These results demonstrate that trapped-ion repeater-node technology can operate over existing city-scale fiber infrastructure and represent a step toward distributed quantum repeater networks.
2610.27854.why: Two ions in one cavity act as a repeater node, linking photons across 17 km of city fiber at 81.6% Bell-state fidelity.

eli5.plain: They built one middle station of a quantum repeater from two trapped ions and used it to entangle photons sent over a real 17 km city fiber.
eli5.how: Each ion emits a photon entangled with it into a shared cavity; one photon travels the long fiber, and a joint operation on the two ions swaps the entanglement onto the two photons.
eli5.matters: This is the deployed-fiber version of the node-to-node state transfer microwave networks are chasing; its loss and fidelity budget is a benchmark for any transducer-based superconducting link.
eli5.caveat: One node, 81.6% fidelity and a low success rate; a useful repeater chain needs several nodes beating direct transmission, which this does not yet show.

2610.31283.title: High-fidelity entanglement of two spectrally-distinct solid state emitters
2610.31283.abstract: Solid state quantum emitters with electronic spin properties can be entangled using optical interferometric which-path erasure techniques that rely on identical frequencies and linewidths of the emitters. This promises a powerful, fast and scalable platform for quantum technologies. Using current protocols, a pair of emitters embedded in a waveguide interferometer can be deterministically prepared in a maximally entangled state. However, the amount of entanglement diminishes rapidly with increasing separation of the emission lines and variations in the linewidths of the emitters. Solid state emitters such as quantum dots are subject to intrinsic variations in the fabrication process. Therefore, manufacturing the required number of identical emitters on a chip is not scalable. In this Letter, we present a method that uses readily available pairs of entangled photons to entangle solid state emitters with large transition frequency separations and linewidth variations, circumventing the need to fabricate optically identical emitters. We demonstrate a concurrence of C = 0.95 for typical quantum dots using narrowband photon inputs.
2610.31283.why: Feeding entangled photon pairs into two mismatched quantum dots entangles them at concurrence 0.95 despite different frequencies and linewidths.

eli5.plain: They propose a way to entangle two solid-state emitters that do not emit the same colour, by giving each a photon from an entangled pair instead of erasing which-path information.
eli5.how: Each emitter absorbs one photon of a pre-entangled narrowband pair, so the entanglement is imported rather than created by interfering identical emissions; mismatch then matters far less.
eli5.matters: Superconducting qubits are never identical either; importing entanglement from a shaped two-mode source is a protocol that maps onto microwave nodes with frequency spread.
eli5.caveat: Simulation only, with narrowband entangled photons assumed available at the right frequencies; absorption efficiency and source brightness set the real rate.

2610.28057.title: Optimal Quantum-Circuit Synthesis and Implementation of General Unitaries with Parallelized Bitstring-Conditioned Rotations
2610.28057.abstract: We theoretically introduce a quantum-circuit synthesis protocol to realize any $n$-qubit transformation $U\in U(2^n)$, up to a diagonal. The resulting circuit is directly native to and optimal in gate count and depth for systems where bitstring-conditioned rotations with tunable angle and axis, $C^{(n-1)}R(θ,φ)$, form the set of native operations. Subsequently, we suggest how this protocol can be implemented in a few-mode superconducting circuit, and experimentally demonstrate the method for the smallest nontrivial case, i.e., for two qubits. We report an average gate fidelity of 97.6 % for Haar-random two-qubit unitaries up to phase shifts in the computational basis. Importantly, these results suggest that multimode devices, such as those in the multimon or multiunimon families may become competitive with qubit-array networks for general-unitary implementations for qubit counts as low as three.
2610.28057.why: Gate-count-optimal synthesis of any n-qubit unitary from bitstring-conditioned rotations, demonstrated at 97.6% on Haar-random two-qubit unitaries.

eli5.plain: A recipe for building any multi-qubit operation from a special kind of native gate, tested on two superconducting qubits.
eli5.how: If the hardware can rotate one qubit conditioned on the exact state of all others, any unitary decomposes into the minimum number of such rotations; a few-mode circuit provides them.
eli5.matters: Native multi-controlled gates could cut circuit depth compared with CNOT-based compilation.
eli5.caveat: Only the two-qubit case is demonstrated, and 97.6% is well below standard two-qubit gate fidelities.

2610.28732.title: Interacting quantum reference frames
2610.28732.abstract: We formulate quantum reference frames within the Dirac quantization of gauge theories, where physical states are obtained from a kinematical Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$ by group averaging. We assume the gauge group $G$ is unimodular, and we define a quantum reference frame as a system of coherent states associated with a group $G_R$ of frame orientations acting on a tensor factor of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. In direct analogy with the Faddeev-Popov procedure in path integrals, we show that the physical inner product can be written in terms of a choice of frame orientation with an appropriate operator measure, but that the physical Hilbert space is independent of this choice of frame. This yields a generalization of the Page-Wootters reduction map used to define conditional states and conditional probabilities of measurement outcomes given a frame orientation. These probabilities correspond to the expectation values of relational Dirac observables obtained from generalizations of previously considered relativization maps. Our main result is that the map that implements a change of frame is unitary, even when $G$ does not act as a tensor-product representation across a factorization of $\mathcal{H}_{\rm kin}$. The formalism therefore accommodates interactions between reference frames and the systems described relative to them. We apply this formalism to temporal frames, showing that a unitary Schrödinger equation emerges for an interacting clock and system, and that a previously reported time-nonlocal Schrödinger equation is recovered in an appropriate limit. With this, problems of non-unitarity are avoided by the use of the gauge-fixing measure in the physical inner product. We also discuss the case of interacting spatial frames, where the known correspondence between coherence in one frame and entanglement in another is shown to depend on the coupling.
2610.28732.why: Frame changes stay unitary even with interacting reference frames, recovering a unitary clock-system Schrödinger equation.

eli5.plain: They extend the theory of quantum reference frames so that the 'ruler' or 'clock' can interact with what it measures, and show switching viewpoints is still a reversible operation.
eli5.how: Physical states come from averaging over a gauge group; choosing a frame orientation is like gauge fixing in path integrals, and the resulting change-of-frame map is unitary.
eli5.matters: It addresses whether time measured by a physical, interacting clock gives sensible quantum dynamics, a question underlying relational readings of quantum mechanics.
eli5.caveat: Formal and restricted to unimodular gauge groups; no experiment is proposed, and the interacting examples are simple models.

2610.30056.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
2610.30056.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum gates that combine short duration, high fidelity, and robustness to noise. As quantum processors scale, robustness becomes increasingly important because exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration of individual gates become impractical. We present a comprehensive optimal-control framework for controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons that systematically accounts for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors and realistic decoherence mechanisms, including energy relaxation and dephasing. Using smooth, single-shot flux pulses, we obtain 12-ns CZ gates---close to the theoretical speed limit of 11.6 ns---with intrinsic errors suppressed to the $2\times10^{-5}$ level. We construct dephasing noise models, calibrated against published experimental measurements, that capture fast dephasing from room-temperature control electronics and slow dephasing from $1/f$ flux noise. Using these models, we identify dephasing sweet spots that suppress sensitivity to dephasing noise. We further exploit transmon asymmetry as a design parameter to access distinct noise-resilient operating regimes. These results establish an experimentally applicable framework for balancing gate speed, fidelity, and noise robustness while reducing characterization and recalibration overhead.
2610.30056.why: Optimal-control flux pulses give 12 ns CZ gates near the 11.6 ns speed limit with errors suppressed under realistic decoherence.

eli5.plain: Theory for the fastest possible high-fidelity two-qubit gate between tunable transmons.
eli5.how: Smooth single flux pulses are optimised against the full transmon Hamiltonian including leakage, relaxation and dephasing.
eli5.matters: Shorter gates lose less to decoherence; a 12 ns CZ would be among the fastest proposed.
eli5.caveat: Simulation only; flux-line distortions and calibration drift are added in part II, but neither paper is an experiment.

W7221906196.title: Population-Based Discrimination of Classical and Few-Photon Microwave Fields with a Flux-Tunable Transmon Qudit
W7221906196.abstract: Interactions between few-photon microwave fields and superconducting artificial atoms provide a method to study photon statistics and manipulate quantum states for photonic quantum information processing. Superconducting transmons couple to microwave fields through an anharmonic ladder of energy levels, producing a response beyond the two-level description. Here, we propose and analyze a detector based on a flux-tunable transmon qudit in circuit quantum electrodynamics. Within a Kerr-type model, we calculate its population response to classical-field excitation and quantized Fock and coherent states. In the four-photon example, a selected detuning produces periodic, nearly complete transfer to the fourth transmon level for a Fock input, while a coherent input of equal mean energy gives a population of approximately 0.2 at the same interaction time. In the linear regime, we derive a target-population bound for classical inputs. From single-tone and two-tone spectroscopy, analyzed using the cosine transmon Hamiltonian, we extract circuit parameters and resolve higher transitions. Ramsey interferometry characterizes dephasing on the fundamental transition. We propose a detection protocol combining flux-selected interaction with dispersive population readout. Our results establish a population-based framework for microwave-state discrimination using a superconducting artificial atom.
W7221906196.why: Proposes reading few-photon microwave statistics from transmon-qudit level populations, separating Fock from coherent inputs via a tuned detuning.

eli5.plain: A theory proposal for telling apart a classical microwave pulse and a pulse with a fixed number of photons by looking at which energy levels of a transmon end up occupied.
eli5.how: The transmon's unequally spaced levels respond differently to each photon number; at a chosen detuning a four-photon Fock state pumps population almost completely up the ladder, while a coherent state smears it out.
eli5.matters: Photon-number-resolving detection of itinerant microwave light is scarce; a transmon used as a multi-level counter is cheap to build with existing hardware.
eli5.caveat: Pure Kerr-model calculation, no decoherence-limited device or real propagating pulse shapes; whether the contrast survives T1 and imperfect absorption is open.

2610.27743.title: Multimode Parametric Amplifier for K-Band Quantum Measurements
2610.27743.abstract: We demonstrate K-band nondegenerate three-wave-mixing amplification in a multimode resonator comprising an array of 500 SNAILs. Pairing K-band signal modes with lower-frequency internal idler modes enables 20 dB of gain continuously from 19.6 to 25.6 GHz with pump frequencies below 32.2 GHz. At 20 dB gain, the 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 2.6 to 11.7 MHz, and the input-referred 1-dB compression power reaches -100.9 dBm. In the 20-22 GHz band, the average added noise is 0.73 quanta. A two-mode nondegenerate parametric amplification model describes the measured gain response and gain-bandwidth behavior, while a multimode Kerr model captures the overall compression scale. Our amplifier provides a practical solution for implementing a state-of-the-art readout of superconducting qubits in the K-band.
2610.27743.why: A 500-SNAIL multimode amplifier gives 20 dB gain across 19.6–25.6 GHz with 0.73 quanta added noise, near-quantum-limited K-band amplification.

eli5.plain: They built a near-quantum-limited microwave amplifier that works at about 20–26 GHz, far above the usual 4–8 GHz band.
eli5.how: A long chain of 500 SNAIL nonlinear elements forms a resonator with many modes; pumping pairs a high-frequency signal mode with a lower-frequency internal idler mode to amplify it.
eli5.matters: Higher-frequency qubits and photons are less sensitive to thermal noise; any K-band quantum-optics experiment needs an amplifier like this to read out weak fields.
eli5.caveat: Instantaneous bandwidth is only 2.6–11.7 MHz and saturation is at −101 dBm, so it is tunable rather than broadband and not yet multiplexing-ready.

W7221516464.title: Flux-tunable transmon with an Al/AlO x /4Hb-TaS2 Josephson junction
W7221516464.abstract: Incorporating van der Waals (vdW) superconductors into Josephson elements extends circuit-QED beyond conventional Al/AlOx/Al junctions, enabling microwave probes of unconventional condensates and subgap excitations. We realize a flux-tunable transmon whose nonlinear inductive element is an Al/AlOx/4Hb-TaS2 Josephson junction, with a tunnel barrier formed by full in situ oxidation of ultrathin Al layers on an exfoliated 4Hb-TaS2 flake in a process compatible with standard transmon fabrication. In a three-dimensional copper cavity, the device shows a SQUID-like flux-dependent spectrum that is well reproduced by a dressed transmon–cavity Hamiltonian in the transmon regime. We measure sub-microsecond energy relaxation (T1=0.08–0.69 μs), while Ramsey measurements indicate dephasing faster than our 16 ns resolution. A naive Ambegaokar–Baratoff comparison using room-temperature junction resistances gives a suppressed effective energy scale; however, cross-sectional TEM reveals an amorphous region at the TaS2 interface, most likely produced by the pre-deposition ion-milling step. We therefore attribute the suppressed EJRn product primarily to a non-ideal hybrid interface. This work demonstrates the integration of 4Hb-TaS2 into a circuit-QED device and establishes an interface-optimization baseline for future edge-sensitive designs targeting boundary and subgap degrees of freedom in vdW superconductors.
W7221516464.why: A transmon with an Al/AlOx/4Hb-TaS2 junction works in a 3D cavity, bringing a van der Waals superconductor into standard circuit QED.

eli5.plain: They made a transmon qubit whose junction is half aluminium, half an exotic layered superconductor, and it behaves like a normal transmon.
eli5.how: Ultrathin aluminium is oxidised on an exfoliated 4Hb-TaS2 flake to form the tunnel barrier; the spectrum in a copper cavity matches a dressed transmon model.
eli5.matters: Transmons become a microwave probe of unconventional superconductors, and new junction materials might reduce the defects that limit coherence.
eli5.caveat: Coherence is sub-microsecond, so this is a materials probe, not a better qubit.

2610.32154.title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
2610.32154.abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two \SI{10}{\um}-long devices with widths of \SI{3.2}{\um} and \SI{6.4}{\um} are characterized under pulsed \SI{515}{nm} excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to \(n=8\). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to \(n=7\) and \(n=8\), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is \(2.15\), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of \(99.6\%\). The EMG exponential-tail parameter \(τ_n\) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter \(μ_n\) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.
2610.32154.why: Wide NbN microstrip detectors resolve up to eight photons from arrival-time shifts alone, with neighbouring peaks separating better at higher number.

eli5.plain: They show that a wide superconducting strip detector tells you how many photons hit it from how early it clicks, up to eight photons.
eli5.how: More photons trigger the superconducting-to-normal switch faster; in wide strips the arrival-time peaks for n and n+1 photons stay well separated instead of crowding together.
eli5.matters: Photon-number resolution from timing, with no extra readout hardware, is the same idea one wants for microwave counters; it also shows how geometry changes vortex-driven switching.
eli5.caveat: Optical photons at 515 nm and a phenomenological model; peak assignment relies on fitting, and fidelity is quoted only for adjacent pairs at equal priors.

2610.28749.title: Bias-Preserving Entanglement of Kerr-Cat Qubits with an ATS Coupler
2610.28749.abstract: Kerr-cat qubits offer a hardware-efficient route to fault-tolerant quantum computing by suppressing bit-flip errors exponentially, while phase-flip errors increase only linearly with the mean photon number. To maintain this protection, entangling operations must be bias-preserving, ensuring that phase-flip errors occurring during the gate do not propagate into bit-flip errors. In this paper, we propose an asymmetrically threaded SQUID (ATS) parametric coupler to implement high-fidelity, bias-preserving entangling gates between Kerr-cat qubits. By engineering a photon-number asymmetry between the control and target modes, we enable fast gate operations that suppress non-adiabatic leakage without complex pulse shaping. Through numerical simulations of the full circuit Hamiltonian, we demonstrate a bias-preserving CX gate achieving 99.69% fidelity in the absence of photon loss for a gate duration of 50 ns. Under a single-photon loss rate of 100 kHz, our protocol yields a noise bias of 9922, exceeding the noise bias of a naive non-bias-preserving CX implementation by approximately a factor of 570. These results support the ATS coupler as a valuable building block for concatenated cat-qubit architectures.
2610.28749.why: Simulated ATS coupler gives a 50 ns bias-preserving CX between Kerr cats at 99.69% fidelity and noise bias near 10^4.

eli5.plain: They design a coupler that entangles two cat qubits without spoiling the property that makes them attractive: bit flips stay rare.
eli5.how: An asymmetrically threaded SQUID drives a parametric interaction; using different photon numbers in control and target modes speeds the gate while avoiding leakage, without pulse shaping.
eli5.matters: Bias-preserving gates are the missing piece for concatenated cat-qubit architectures pursued by AWS and Alice&Bob; the ATS is a hardware they already use.
eli5.caveat: Numerical simulation of an idealised circuit; real devices add dephasing, thermal photons and parameter drift not modelled here.

2610.29804.title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
2610.29804.abstract: In quantum mechanics, conservation laws are usually understood only statistically and only in the context of unitary evolution: during such evolution, if an observable commutes with the Hamiltonian, its expectation value and Born-rule probability distribution remain unchanged. Individual measurement outcomes, however, disrupt even this weak form of statistical conservation. Recently, though, it has been argued that a stronger, non-statistical form of conservation, valid at the level of individual measurement outcomes, can be recovered. The proposal relies on the claim that any superposition of eigenstates of a conserved quantity must ultimately be prepared relative to another physical system, which serves as the relevant reference frame and remains correlated with the system being prepared. On this enlarged description, the change observed in the measured system is claimed to be exactly compensated by an opposite change in the preparer, thereby restoring conservation at the level of individual measurement outcomes. We analyze this proposal and argue that it faces significant conceptual difficulties. We show that the proposed mechanism is not adequately justified and, moreover, does not establish conservation in individual measurement outcomes as claimed.
2610.29804.why: Critique shows the proposed outcome-by-outcome conservation via correlated preparers is unjustified and does not deliver what it claims.

eli5.plain: They examine a recent claim that energy and other conserved quantities hold in every single measurement, not just on average, and argue it fails.
eli5.how: The claim relies on the preparing apparatus absorbing the change; they show the bookkeeping does not follow and the mechanism is not justified by the theory.
eli5.matters: Whether conservation laws survive collapse is a direct question about what measurement does, relevant to anyone reading a single-shot qubit readout as a physical event.
eli5.caveat: A critique, not a new result; defenders may refine the original proposal rather than abandon it.

2610.30857.title: All-photonic millimeter-wave and terahertz signal core at room and cryogenic temperatures
2610.30857.abstract: Millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies offer new opportunities for high-capacity communications, sensing, and quantum systems, but electronic signal chains above 100 GHz are limited by weak sources, noisy receivers, and lossy interconnects. Photonic approaches mitigate these constraints by enabling chip-scale high-frequency components, yet existing implementations generally retain lossy off-chip electrical or free-space links, hindering dense and compact integration for cryogenic or space-constrained settings. Here, we show a monolithic lithium tantalate photonic chip, termed a signal core, which generates, modulates, routes, and detects continuous-wave signals at discrete frequencies between 100 GHz and 2.5 THz. The architecture integrates high-frequency functional modules on chip and uses exclusively fiber-based optical interfaces. Bidirectional coherent electro-optic conversion enables signal generation, detection, and nanosecond-scale amplitude and phase modulation, while micro-coplanar striplines interconnect the modules into an end-to-end signal chain on a single chip. Our modules achieve single-photon electro-optic coupling rates of g_0/2π=10 kHz and peak drive-power-normalized photon-flux conversion efficiencies of 1.0%/mW for generation and 0.5%/mW for detection. It also operates at 4 K in a dilution refrigerator through the same fiber-only optical links. Together, these capabilities establish an all-photonic platform for millimeter-wave-to-terahertz systems and offer a broadly applicable architecture for applications constrained by electrical-interconnect loss, heat load, and footprint.
2610.30857.why: A lithium tantalate chip generates, modulates and detects 0.1–2.5 THz signals through fibre only, and still works at 4 K.

eli5.plain: They built a photonic chip that makes, steers and detects millimetre-wave to terahertz signals, fed only by optical fibres, and ran it inside a dilution refrigerator.
eli5.how: Electro-optic conversion turns light into high-frequency electrical signals and back, with on-chip striplines wiring the blocks together so no coax enters the cryostat.
eli5.matters: Fibre-only control of a cold stage is exactly the heat-load and wiring problem of scaling superconducting processors, and the electro-optic coupling numbers are relevant to transduction.
eli5.caveat: Conversion efficiencies near 1%/mW are far from quantum-limited, and the frequencies are above the few-GHz band superconducting qubits use.

2610.30681.title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. II. System-parameter uncertainties and overall errors
2610.30681.abstract: In the companion paper (Part I), we developed an optimal-control framework to suppress intrinsic and decoherence-induced errors in controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons. Here, we extend this framework to incorporate uncertainties in coupling strength, anharmonicities, and zero-flux qubit frequencies, enabling the design of high-fidelity gates robust against noise and parameter uncertainties. We classify these uncertainties by whether they perturb the off-diagonal coupling strengths or the diagonal detunings of the Hamiltonian, and we identify distinct suppression mechanisms for each class. Coupling errors are mitigated through dynamical decoupling induced by strong detuning modulation. For a 30-ns gate, this strategy reduces the coupling error to $6.21\times10^{-7}$ and tolerates coupling-strength uncertainties up to $2π\times4$ MHz while keeping total gate infidelity below $10^{-3}$. Detuning errors are minimized near a symmetric-detuning operating point that balances the two dominant leakage-mediated interactions. A 24-ns gate operated near this point tolerates individual uncertainties of up to $2π\times5$ MHz in each relevant diagonal parameter under the same infidelity threshold. We further optimize gate performance under realistic conditions where intrinsic errors, decoherence, and parameter uncertainties coexist across six representative stages of progressively improving hardware performance. The resulting stage-specific controls achieve lower infidelity and greater robustness. Together with the companion study (Part I), this framework offers a practical approach to balance speed, fidelity, and robustness while reducing the need for exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.
2610.30681.why: Extends the 12 ns CZ design to parameter uncertainty, separating coupling errors from detuning errors and suppressing each differently.

eli5.plain: Part II of the fast-CZ theory: making the gate still work when you do not know the device parameters exactly.
eli5.how: Errors in coupling are cancelled by dynamical-decoupling-like structure in the pulse, while frequency errors are handled by separate robustness terms.
eli5.matters: Robustness to fabrication spread is what makes a gate usable without per-pair tuning.
eli5.caveat: Theory and numerics, same caveat as part I.

2610.27471.title: Engineering \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two remote superconducting qubits via a multimode waveguide
2610.27471.abstract: Waveguides provide a flexible platform for long-range interactions between superconducting qubits. Here, we study how to engineer the effective \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions between two qubits via qubit frequency assignments and multimode interference determined by the mode configuration and standing-wave parities of a finite multimode waveguide. For a single-mode waveguide, we find that \(XY\) and \(ZZ\) interactions cannot be simultaneously suppressed to zero and the residual qubit-qubit coupling always exists. For example, the \(XY\) interaction may be suppressed to a negligible level when two qubits and the waveguide mode satisfy the two-photon resonant condition, but the \(ZZ\) interaction cannot be switched off. For multimode configurations within the central dispersive window, the engineered interaction types are very different for odd and even numbers of modes. Even-mode configurations can readily produce strong \(XY\) interactions, whereas odd-mode configurations can strongly suppress the \(XY\) interaction while retaining a finite \(ZZ\) interaction. Full-Hamiltonian simulations of minimal two- and three-mode configurations confirm \(XY\)-dominated SWAP dynamics and \(ZZ\)-dominated CZ-type dynamics, respectively. These results establish a frequency assignment criterion of qubits and waveguide modes for selectively engineering long-range qubit-qubit interaction types induced by the waveguide with finite multimode.
2610.27471.why: Shows XY and ZZ couplings between remote qubits on a multimode waveguide can be nulled together only using several modes' standing-wave parities.

eli5.plain: Theory for how two distant qubits on a long resonant waveguide interact, and how to switch off their unwanted crosstalk.
eli5.how: Each waveguide mode contributes a coupling whose sign depends on whether the mode's standing wave is symmetric or antisymmetric at the two qubits; picking qubit frequencies between modes lets these contributions cancel.
eli5.matters: Long-range waveguide links are a route to remote entanglement; knowing when residual ZZ is unavoidable tells you how to place qubit frequencies.
eli5.caveat: A finite, standing-wave waveguide rather than an open line, and no experiment; disorder and loss are not the focus.

2610.32885.title: Polarization-encoded photon statistics for counting dipole emitters
2610.32885.abstract: Counting the emitters within a diffraction-limited region is a prerequisite for localizing overlapping molecules. Under pulsed excitation, each molecule emits at most one photon per pulse, so photon-number-resolved detection can count emitters without resolving them. But the required number of pulses grows steeply with the emitter number. Here we show that polarization, conventionally used to measure the orientations of dipole emitters, also carries information on their number. Because mean polarization-resolved signals are unchanged when every emitter is replaced by multiple dimmer copies, this information resides in the photon statistics within each pulse, which polarization reshapes in two ways. Linearly polarized excitation at three angles increases the sub-Poissonian deficit of the photon count by a factor of 1.5 for any emitter orientation, and detection in four polarization channels reveals the emitter number through how the photons of multiphoton pulses are distributed among the channels. Maximum-likelihood simulations for two to five emitters of unknown orientations and brightnesses show that three-angle excitation reduces the required number of pulses by about 2.3-fold, close to the predicted $1.5^2=2.25$, and that adding four-channel detection raises the reduction to as much as 4.8-fold. These gains require only polarization optics added to photon-number-resolved detection.
2610.32885.why: Polarized excitation and four-channel detection let photon statistics count overlapping emitters with up to 4.8 times fewer pulses.

eli5.plain: They show that measuring the polarization of photons, not just how many arrive, makes it much faster to count how many molecules sit in one blurry spot.
eli5.how: Each molecule gives at most one photon per pulse; polarized excitation deepens the sub-Poissonian dip, and how multi-photon pulses split across polarization channels reveals the emitter number.
eli5.matters: It is a clean example of extracting emitter number from photon-number statistics by adding a mode degree of freedom, a trick that carries to counting artificial atoms in a waveguide.
eli5.caveat: Simulations only, for two to five emitters, assuming good photon-number-resolving detectors.

2610.31729.title: Mutual Information Across Quantum Reference Frame Perspectives
2610.31729.abstract: In quantum information theory, standard notions typically presuppose a fixed partition of the world into subsystems, encoded in a tensor product structure of the Hilbert space. Yet, in some scenarios, the subsystem structure is not uniquely fixed. A case in point is the description of subsystems relative to different quantum reference frames (QRFs), where the tensor product structure, although fixed in a specific QRF, changes across different QRFs. Such a relativity of subsystems underlies many interesting features of QRFs, such as the relativity of entanglement, entropy, and coherence. It also raises a broader question: how do we compare the information across different subsystem perspectives, especially when the corresponding subsystem algebras overlap? Here, we propose a notion of quantum mutual information across different QRF perspectives, which captures the correlations between subsystems relative to different frames of reference. To do so, we focus on an algebraic definition of subsystems. Studying in detail the union and overlap between subsystem algebras relative to different QRFs, we find that the usual definition of mutual information in terms of the chain law overcounts the information associated to the overlap. Based on this insight, we propose a modified chain law and show that the resulting notion of mutual information satisfies subadditivity and connects naturally to other measures found in the literature [1]. Our investigations not only provide a way to quantify the relation between different QRF perspectives from an information-theoretic point of view but also sheds light on some important features of quantum information in absence of a fixed tensor product structure.
2610.31729.why: Defines mutual information between subsystems seen from different quantum reference frames, correcting overcounting via a modified chain rule.

eli5.plain: They define how much two observers using different quantum reference frames 'share' information, when they disagree about how the world splits into parts.
eli5.how: Subsystems are defined by operator algebras; when algebras from two frames overlap, the usual chain rule double-counts, so they modify it and recover subadditivity.
eli5.matters: It addresses why the tensor-product split is not given a priori, which bears on what entanglement between a qubit and its environment even means.
eli5.caveat: Information-theoretic and definitional; it proposes a measure rather than proving something about the physical world.

2610.29901.title: Superconducting parametric amplifiers based on arrays of unequal Josephson junction elements
2610.29901.abstract: Impedance matching is a crucial feature of an amplifier used to increase its instantaneous bandwidth and is typically achieved using static LC resonators. Here we show an approach to impedance matching in parametric amplifiers using arrays of unequal Josephson-junction-based elements (rf/dc SQUIDs, SNAILs, etc). The elements act either as small-footprint flux-tunable inductors forming an impedance-matching circuit, or 'active' amplifier elements which result in amplifier gain. We develop an analytical theory describing these systems, predicting a quasi-non-periodic amplifier frequency and gain modulation with applied flux and the broadening of gain bandwidths. We demonstrate this in devices using arrays of flux-focused SNAILs where flux biasing varies across the array. We find instantaneous bandwidths of 200 MHz with $>$17 dB of gain centred at $\sim$5.4 GHz in a device without a static impedance matcher. This broadening of amplifier bandwidth is stable with $>$100 MHz bandwidth at 17 dB gain across $>$1.2 GHz tunable bandwidth. Our analytical model captures flux dependence and qualitatively reproduces gain-bandwidths giving confidence in our understanding of these systems and allowing operational figures of merit to be optimised in future devices.
2610.29901.why: Unequal-junction arrays double as tunable impedance-matching networks and gain elements, broadening paramp bandwidth with flux-dependent gain modulation.

eli5.plain: A new way to make Josephson parametric amplifiers wider-band, by making the junctions in the chain deliberately different from each other.
eli5.how: Some of the junction-based elements act as compact tunable inductors that match the amplifier to the 50-ohm line, while others provide the parametric gain; theory and devices show broader gain bands.
eli5.matters: Wideband, near-quantum-limited amplification is the first stage of every itinerant-photon measurement in circuit QED.
eli5.caveat: The abstract does not quote noise temperature or compression, the numbers that decide whether it beats existing impedance-matched paramps.

2610.24167.title: Probing wetting and solidification dynamics of neon thin films with a high-$T_c$ superconducting circuit
2610.24167.abstract: Integrating condensed noble gases with superconducting circuits offers new opportunities for operating hybrid quantum devices. In particular, electrons on solid neon have recently emerged as exceptionally coherent charge qubits, however the growth of the underlying neon films on patterned devices remains poorly controlled. We monitor neon films near the triple point using a multimode resonator fabricated from high-$T_c$ YBCO, which remains superconducting at temperatures where the liquid phase exists and whose geometry sets a thickness-sensing window near 1 $μ$m. In the liquid state we observe rich film dynamics: uniform wetting that saturates near 20 nm, drainage of thicker films, and spontaneous thickness oscillations, reflecting the extreme sensitivity of thick films in this regime. A galvanic connection to our sensing volume enables in-situ electrostatic tuning of the liquid film thickness. Statistics of freezing the neon across various liquid levels reveal variations of the solid film thickness by approximately an order of magnitude. We also observe a two-fold increase in the quality factor of the resonators at the level of $10^3$ with added neon and rule out dielectric loss as the limiting factor. Our results demonstrate that hermetic packaging facilitates the investigation of both rich non-equilibrium fluid dynamics and the impact of condensed noble gas films on microwave loss in superconducting circuits, but may not be the best modality for growing solid neon films with precisely controlled thickness.
2610.24167.why: A YBCO multimode resonator watches neon films wet, drain and solidify near the triple point, informing electron-on-neon qubit fabrication.

eli5.plain: They used a high-temperature superconducting resonator as a thickness gauge to watch thin neon films grow, flow and freeze.
eli5.how: The neon changes the resonator's frequencies; YBCO stays superconducting at the 25 K where liquid neon exists, so they can watch the liquid phase directly.
eli5.matters: Electrons on solid neon are among the most coherent charge qubits; controlling the neon film is the bottleneck for making them reproducibly.
eli5.caveat: Film physics only, no qubit measured; the sensing window sits around 1 µm, much thicker than the films qubits use.

2610.31452.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
2610.31452.abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.
2610.31452.why: Nanopillar metasurface on a thin membrane reaches 99.82% reflectivity while hosting a mechanical mode with Q·f of 2×10^14 Hz.

eli5.plain: They made a mirror that is both highly reflective and a very clean mechanical resonator, two goals that usually fight each other.
eli5.how: Pillars on a thin membrane form a photonic crystal that reflects a tightly focused beam, while the same pattern acts as a phononic crystal that isolates one low-loss vibration mode.
eli5.matters: Ultracoherent membranes are candidates for microwave-optical transducers and mechanical memories coupled to superconducting circuits.
eli5.caveat: Demonstrated at 1550 nm and room temperature; no cavity optomechanics or quantum-regime operation is shown yet.

2610.28046.title: Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
2610.28046.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides an ultrafast probe of quantum materials, yet conventional spectral observables do not generally furnish a common signature of band topology. Here we show that quantum-light-driven HHG opens an additional information channel through the photon statistics of the emitted harmonics. Using the Haldane Chern insulator and the time-reversal-invariant Kane-Mele topological insulator, we calculate helicity-resolved equal-time intensity correlations and identify a common enhancement of high-order harmonic correlations in the topological phases. For the Haldane model, a dichroic correlation constructed from opposite helicity channels reverses sign with the Chern number. These signatures originate from the distinct nonlinear response sampled by quantum fluctuations of the driving field and are absent from the corresponding mean harmonic spectra as a common classifier. Our results establish photon-correlation spectroscopy as a route to interrogate topological matter with quantum light and provide a bridge between strong-field solid-state physics and quantum optics.
2610.28046.why: Harmonics driven by quantum light carry intensity correlations that flip sign with the Chern number, absent from the mean spectrum.

eli5.plain: They predict that the photon statistics of high harmonics, generated in a material by quantum light, can reveal whether the material is topological.
eli5.how: Fluctuations of a non-classical drive sample the material's nonlinear response; correlations between helicity channels pick up the band topology even when average spectra do not.
eli5.matters: It is an example of photon correlations as a probe that mean intensities miss, the same logic as g2 measurements on circuit emitters.
eli5.caveat: Model calculations on idealised lattice models; the needed bright quantum drives for HHG and correlation measurements at high harmonics are experimentally hard.

2610.26465.title: The Four-Qubit Hyperbolic Quadric Has Contextuality Degree 315
2610.26465.abstract: The contextuality degree of a set of Pauli contexts is the least number of contexts that every noncontextual $\pm1$ assignment violates. For the four-qubit hyperbolic quadric $\mathcal{Q}^{+}(7,2)$, with $135$ points and $1575$ lines as contexts, Muller et al. conjectured from heuristic searches that the degree is $315$ and that the violated contexts of every optimal assignment form a dual polar space $DW(5,2)$. We prove both conjectures. The lower bound has a short proof by hand: every doily ($GQ(2,2)$) of the quadric contains ten Peres-Mermin grids covering each of its lines four times, so every assignment violates at least three of its fifteen lines, and averaging over the doilies gives $1575/5=315$. The equality case is local: an assignment is optimal exactly when it violates one ruling of one grid in every doily. Using this as a SAT encoding, we show that there are exactly $240$ optimal violated sets, one orbit of $\mathrm{O}^+(8,2)$, each isomorphic to $DW(5,2)$. The same argument gives the first lower bounds $\lceil L/5\rceil$ for all quadrics with $L$ lines in $N\ge4$ qubits. The degree theorem is kernel-checked in Lean 4, and the completeness of the enumeration is certified by a DRAT proof checked by the verified checker cake_lpr.
2610.26465.why: Proves the four-qubit hyperbolic quadric has contextuality degree 315, with a hand proof plus Lean and DRAT certificates.

eli5.plain: They prove exactly how badly any classical, pre-assigned-values model must fail for a specific large set of four-qubit Pauli measurements.
eli5.how: Each sub-structure contains Peres–Mermin grids forcing at least three violations; averaging gives the lower bound 315, and a SAT search shows all optimal patterns are one symmetric family.
eli5.matters: A sharp contextuality count gives a target for experiments testing noncontextual hidden variables on multi-qubit processors.
eli5.caveat: Mostly a combinatorial result; its physical reading is the standard Kochen–Specker one, and noise thresholds for an experiment are not derived.

2610.30473.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
2610.30473.abstract: We review what it means for a relativistic particle to be localized and argue that the most useful approach is through local measurement. This perspective ties localization directly to relativistic causality and measurable outcomes in spacetime. Strict localization in quantum field theory is formalized by states that give the same expectation value as vacuum for all local observables outside some spacetime region. With this formalism, single photons cannot be strictly localized, but coherent states can. The structure and interpretation of local observables and local operator algebras are discussed in connection with the Reeh-Schlieder theorem. Since probabilities of local measurement outcomes cannot vanish in vacuum, particle detection events must be phrased carefully. Key characteristics of strictly localized states are surveyed alongside concrete strategies for constructing them. The relationship between localization, causality, and on-demand sources is analyzed, finding that strictly localized states can represent localized, propagating information in quantum field theory. Explicit examples of localized photonic states are presented with an emphasis on quantum optics, including states that approximate single photons and (entangled) Bell states.
2610.30473.why: Review argues localization must be defined by local measurements: single photons cannot be strictly localized, coherent states can.

eli5.plain: A review of what it means for a photon to be 'somewhere', built on what local detectors can measure rather than on wavefunctions.
eli5.how: A state is strictly localized if it looks like vacuum to every measurement outside a region; quantum field theory forbids this for single photons but allows it for coherent states.
eli5.matters: Anyone who emits or catches 'a single photon in a wavepacket' uses this language loosely; the review says which statements about on-demand sources survive relativistic causality.
eli5.caveat: A review and conceptual reframing; it adds no new measurement and the operational consequences for lab sources are qualitative.

2610.30686.title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
2610.30686.abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ mediates interactions between $N$ bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of $N^2/e$ with the collective $\langle J_y\rangle$ readout, corresponding to a $4.34\,\mathrm{dB}$ offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small $N-$independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of $N^2/4$ ($6\,\mathrm{dB}$ below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.
2610.30686.why: A central spin mediating a star-shaped bath implements SATIN and butterfly echoes reaching Heisenberg-scaled sensing for any unknown axis.

eli5.plain: They show a sensing protocol that runs time forward and backward through a single central spin to reach near-ideal precision with many bath spins.
eli5.how: Interactions go through one ancilla; reversing them amplifies a small signal, and random collective rotations make it work whatever direction the signal points.
eli5.matters: A qubit coupled to many modes or spins via a common bus is a circuit QED geometry, so the protocol could transfer to a transmon coupled to a spin ensemble.
eli5.caveat: Purely theoretical and noiseless; decoherence and imperfect time reversal will eat into the 4–6 dB offsets quoted.

2610.25471.title: \textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer
2610.25471.abstract: We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.
2610.25471.why: Bunching statistics in any random interferometer certify multiphoton indistinguishability with polynomial runs, even under uniform loss.

eli5.plain: They propose a quick test, run on the experiment itself, of how identical the photons in a big interference experiment really are.
eli5.how: Identical bosons bunch together more than distinguishable ones; averaging bunching signatures over a generic interferometer gives an indistinguishability estimate with polynomial sampling cost.
eli5.matters: Certifying identical photons in situ matters for any multi-photon microwave interference experiment too, where indistinguishability is usually inferred indirectly.
eli5.caveat: The polynomial guarantee is with high probability for Haar-random interferometers and uniform loss; structured devices and nonuniform loss are not covered.

2610.31885.title: Optimal Control of a Fluxonium Circuit with the Q-PRONTO Numerical Method
2610.31885.abstract: Optimizing the control of large quantum systems is a resource-intensive task, where the convergence rate of the underlying iterative schemes is crucial. The recently developed Quantum Projection Operator-Based Newton Method for Trajectory Optimization (Q-PRONTO) offers a unique quadratic convergence for controlling quantum states, while most model-based solvers guarantee only an approximately linear convergence rate. As a proof of concept, here, we design and benchmark single-qubit gates optimized by Q-PRONTO based on the circuit Hamiltonian of a fluxonium superconducting qubit. To ensure that we can apply a long string of arbitrary pulses to the circuit, we modify the firmware associated with the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) by altering its memory allocation. We characterize the performance of the optimal solutions using standard randomized benchmarking and achieve a total error per gate of $6.6\times10^{-4}$.
2610.31885.why: Q-PRONTO, a quadratically convergent optimal-control solver, designs fluxonium single-qubit gates run on hardware through modified firmware.

eli5.plain: A faster-converging pulse optimiser, tested by designing gates for a fluxonium qubit.
eli5.how: A Newton-type method on the full circuit Hamiltonian converges quadratically; firmware changes let the device play long arbitrary pulse strings.
eli5.matters: Fluxonium needs non-standard pulses; faster optimisers shorten calibration.
eli5.caveat: Proof of concept; the abstract gives no fidelity comparison with standard pulses.

2610.27872.title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
2610.27872.abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.
2610.27872.why: Replica calculation gives closed-form growth rates and corrections for moments of random permanents and hafnians, relevant to boson sampling.

2610.27639.title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
2610.27639.abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $π$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|α|^2/(1+|α|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.
2610.27639.why: Phase inversion in seeded biphoton sources flips the stimulated evolution, giving a controllable two-level 'time qubit' with a complementarity law.

2610.27161.title: Allight: A Perfect Photon Collector
2610.27161.abstract: Collecting photons from quantum emitters remains a key limitation in light-matter interaction because conventional lenses collect light only from one direction. Here, we introduce a perfect light collector by inverse-designing a surrounding dielectric structure that encloses the emitter to increase photon-collection efficiency toward unity. Decomposing the device into several refractive interfaces enables emission collection from the full 4$π$ solid angle with adiabatic reshaping into a collimated beam. We experimentally demonstrate, in two dimensions, the ray bending that collimates omnidirectional emission. Our collector transforms current paradigms for highly efficient photon collection from narrowband, cavity-based techniques into experimentally robust, broadband, non-resonant dielectric devices.
2610.27161.why: Inverse-designed dielectric enclosure collects emission from the full 4π solid angle into one beam; ray bending demonstrated only in 2D.

W7222091308.title: Integrated scheme for transferring quantum entanglement via backward acousto-optic polarization conversion in a thin-film lithium niobate resonator
W7222091308.abstract: We present a numerical study of the design of a microwave-to-optical quantum converter based on Brillouin backscattering in a single thin-film lithium niobate racetrack resonator. The conversion involves TE0 to TM0 polarization conversion mediated by an even-parity acoustic mode that can be excited by a conventional symmetric interdigital transducer. Co-localization of the optical and acoustic fields within a single resonator enhances their interaction, while the signal is separated from the strong optical pump by propagation direction, polarization, and frequency. Combining full-vector electromagnetic and acoustic calculations with a pulsed entanglement transfer protocol, we obtain a vacuum coupling of g0/2π = 2 kHz for the designed perimeter and show that cooperativity of C = 1 is achieved with a calculated on-chip pump power of approximately 2.94 μW for Qopt = 107 and Qac = 105. Under these assumptions, the protocol enables entanglement transfer from a superconducting qubit to a flying telecom photon, supporting the proposed architecture as a compact platform for integrated quantum transduction.
W7222091308.why: Simulates microwave-to-optical entanglement transfer via Brillouin backscattering in one thin-film lithium niobate racetrack resonator.

eli5.plain: A design study for a device that converts microwave quantum signals into optical ones using sound waves in a lithium niobate ring.
eli5.how: A microwave drive excites an acoustic wave, which scatters light from one polarization to another; the converted photon travels backwards, separating it from the strong optical pump.
eli5.matters: Transducers like this are how superconducting nodes might eventually be linked over optical fibre.
eli5.caveat: Numerical only, with no superconducting qubit in the loop and no added-noise budget at millikelvin temperatures.

2610.30124.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
2610.30124.abstract: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.
2610.30124.why: Membrane vibrations scatter cavity light into evanescent sidebands that steer free-electron recoil and read out localized forces.

2610.32368.title: Quantum theory of laser noise in coherent-scattering levitated optomechanics
2610.32368.abstract: State purity is a key resource for experimental tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects. Cavity cooling of a levitated nanoparticle via coherent scattering stands out as a strategy to prepare highly pure states of its roto-translational motion. In several cases, though, the performance of cooling by coherent scattering is limited by the classical fluctuations of the laser field. Here we present a quantum theory of coherent-scattering experiments which includes the effect of the laser amplitude and phase noise. We derive a master equation for the noise-averaged particle's dynamics, valid for both center-of-mass and rotational degrees of freedom, and quantify the cooling performance for different levels of noise in state-of-the-art experiments. We compute approximate analytical expressions for the laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon number in both regimes of weak and strong optomechanical coupling. Moreover, our model can be applied to laser noise processes with generic power spectral densities and finite correlation times. This work offers a toolbox to quantify and optimize the state purity in coherent-scattering experiments, and opens new avenues towards the preparation of quantum states with levitated systems.
2610.32368.why: Master equation for laser amplitude and phase noise sets heating rates and phonon floors in coherent-scattering cooling of nanoparticles.
