2610.28596.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
2610.28596.abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell-pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$. Remarkably, this optimal protocol can provide substantial memory reductions over existing heuristic approaches. In particular, for the path graph $P_n$ over $n$ users, Piecemaker protocol requires at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ qubits of peak persistent memory for \textit{every Bell-links generation order}, whereas under the order $(1,2,\ldots,n)$, our protocol requires only one persistent switch qubit. Finally, the same stabilizer-transition framework also provides a direct forward construction for sequential graph-state generation using the minimum number of quantum emitters, equal to the maximum of the height function.
2610.28596.why: Characterises minimum switch memory for graph-state distribution and gives a polynomial protocol needing one qubit for a path graph.

2610.32160.title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
2610.32160.abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.
2610.32160.why: Single-step SU(3) gates give a qutrit Hahn echo extending coherence tenfold and form a three-path atom interferometer.

eli5.plain: They extended the classic spin echo trick to three-level atoms in free fall, keeping them coherent ten times longer and making a three-arm interferometer.
eli5.how: Optimal-control laser pulses rotate all three levels at once, refocusing dephasing; the beam geometry makes the sequence a three-path Mach–Zehnder interferometer.
eli5.matters: Three-path interference is the setting where Born's rule could be tested for higher-order interference; this builds the instrument.
eli5.caveat: No Born-rule test is performed yet; gate fidelity is about 93%.

2610.28204.title: Parallel Teleportation via AME(5,2) States on IBM Quantum Hardware
2610.28204.abstract: The five-qubit Absolutely Maximally Entangled AME$(5,2)$ state, whose every pair of qubits is maximally mixed so that all its information lives in non-local correlations, could in principle serve as a single shared quantum networking resource for teleporting two unknown qubits in parallel (each via its own Bell measurement and Pauli correction). Nonetheless, its hardware implementations remain scarce despite its theoretical importance. Here, we demonstrate parallel teleportation based on a five-qubit absolutely maximally entangled state, AME$(5,2)$, on the superconducting processor ibm_pittsburgh. We construct three-qubit Clifford decoders that extract two Bell pairs using three logical two-qubit gates for each of 60 inequivalent sender-receiver assignments. Using parallelization and classical Pauli frame post-processing, we retain reference-receiver entanglement on both channels after three teleportation rounds. With XY4 dynamical decoupling and the lowest-cost decoder, the final entanglement fidelities are $0.704\pm0.028$ and $0.680\pm0.022$, where uncertainties are pointwise $99\%$ confidence-interval half-widths over eight trials. Their lower bounds exceed the separability threshold of $1/2$. The decoder with lower circuit depth generally retains higher mean fidelity, and XY4 generally improves on XX. These results establish a hardware demonstration of two-channel entanglement transmission through repeated AME-assisted teleportation and provide compact decoding circuits for reconfigurable multipartite communication.
2610.28204.why: Parallel two-qubit teleportation through a five-qubit AME(5,2) state on ibm_pittsburgh, with Clifford decoders extracting two Bell pairs.

2610.24213.title: Generalized Svetlichny Inequalities as a Cross-Platform Benchmark for Quantum Processors
2610.24213.abstract: A cross-platform benchmark should be device-independent yet sensitive to imperfections accumulated during execution. Building on prior work, we formulate and validate a protocol through demonstrations based on generalized Svetlichny inequality violations (a simulation, rather than a loophole-free certification, of multipartite nonlocality) for larger subsystem sizes. We apply it unchanged to three processors, the trapped-ion Marmot and IBEX Q1 (both manufactured by AQT) and the superconducting Euro-Q-Exa System 1 (IQM), using identical GHZ-state circuits with fixed theoretical measurement settings from N=2 to N=10 qubits. Both trapped-ion processors sustain violations up to ten qubits, while the superconducting processor loses them beyond six qubits under unmitigated (raw) conditions; readout-error mitigation recovers violations up to eight qubits, with a substantial fraction of the degradation attributable to measurement imperfections. These processors provide a heterogeneous testbed for validating the protocol's cross-platform applicability and discriminating power, demonstrating its practicality as a common framework for assessing collective quantum performance.
2610.24213.why: Svetlichny-inequality GHZ benchmark: two AQT ion processors violate up to ten qubits, the IQM superconducting system fewer.

2610.31947.title: Noise-Assisted Quantum Entanglement: Memory-Enhanced Coherence in Stochastic Jaynes-Cummings Dynamics
2610.31947.abstract: We investigate qubit entanglement dynamics in a two-qubit cavity system with stochastically fluctuating coupling strength, comparing white noise (Markovian) and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise (non-Markovian) processes. We analytically solve the system dynamics for both Fock and coherent cavity states and systematically characterize how initial qubit configurations affect entanglement generation and preservation. Our results reveal distinct dynamical regimes: in the Fock-state cavity, initial states in the single-excitation subspace generate robust qubit entanglement in decoherence-free subspaces, while initially entangled states in the double-excitation subspace exhibit inevitable decay without protective symmetries. For coherent cavities, we identify a critical photon-number threshold in the intermediate coherent-state amplitude regime where dynamics transition from low-frequency to high-frequency entanglement oscillations, while universal entanglement loss occurs at large amplitudes. Remarkable resilience against entanglement sudden death emerges under strong non-Markovian noise with long correlation times, where repeated revivals occur. These findings establish cavity photon statistics and environmental memory time as key control parameters for engineering qubit entanglement dynamics in qubit-cavity systems, revealing how system-environment correlations govern quantum information preservation.
2610.31947.why: Non-Markovian coupling noise in a two-qubit Jaynes–Cummings model produces entanglement revivals and resists sudden death.

2610.27226.title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
2610.27226.abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.
2610.27226.why: Simulated plasmonic metasurface switches two-photon interference between bunching and antibunching by frequency or geometry.

2610.30998.title: A Personal History in Quantum Foundations: an Oral History Interview
2610.30998.abstract: This oral history interview provides Yakir Aharonov's personal and conceptual recollections from the 1950s to the 2000s, focusing on his academic trajectory, some of his major contributions to quantum foundations, and his perspective on the development of the field. The interview traces Aharonov's academic career through the Technion, University of Bristol, Brandeis University, Yeshiva University, University of South Carolina, Tel Aviv University, George Mason University, and Chapman University. The interview also traces the development of Aharonov's work and collaborations on the EPR paradox, time-energy uncertainty relations, quantum measurement theory, quantum frames of reference, the two-state vector formalism, weak values, protective measurements, and several other contributions. It includes recollections of meetings and discussions with David Bohm, Niels Bohr, John Clauser, Paul Dirac, Rudolf Peierls, Aage Petersen, and Abner Shimony. Also mentioned: David Albert, Jeeva Anandan, Peter Bergmann, Gideon Carmi, Avshalom Elitzur, Dave Finkelstein, Vladimir Fock, Itzhak Kalugai, Ed Lerner, Joel Lebowitz, Stanley Mandelstam, Yuval Ne'eman, Sandu Popescu, Maurice Pryce, Daniel Rohrlich, Nathan Rosen, Joseph Safko, Paul Singer, Daniele Struppa, Leonard Susskind, Lev Vaidman, Chien-Shiung Wu.
2610.30998.why: Oral history of Yakir Aharonov's career, from EPR and time-energy uncertainty to weak values and protective measurement.

eli5.plain: An interview in which Yakir Aharonov recounts how his main ideas in quantum foundations came about.
eli5.how: A historian guides him through his career and collaborations, with recollections of Bohm, Bohr, Dirac and others.
eli5.matters: It gives context for weak values and the two-state vector formalism, which are often used to interpret weak measurements in circuit QED.
eli5.caveat: Personal recollection, not argument; nothing new is claimed about the physics.

2610.24196.title: Nonlocality as a Benchmarking Tool for Quantum Processors
2610.24196.abstract: Benchmarking quantum processors is a central task in every roadmap aimed at quantum advantage. Here, we discuss a benchmarking protocol based on the violation of the Svetlichny inequality, which is designed to simulate genuine multipartite nonlocality. We compare it with Mermin's inequality, and present the results of applying this framework to two different quantum processing units -the superconducting system Garnet (from IQM) and the ion-trap system Marmot (from AQT), testing different families of quantum circuits for three to five qubits under identical experimental conditions. We also run simultaneous triplet tests across the full register, including a comparison between GHZ and linear cluster states, to probe how Svetlichny-inequality violations depend on qubit location and calibration. Our results demonstrate that tests based on genuine multipartite nonlocality provide a powerful tool to characterize the collective performance of quantum devices and to guide their calibration and optimization.
2610.24196.why: Compares Svetlichny and Mermin benchmarks on IQM Garnet and AQT Marmot for three to five qubits, including simultaneous register-wide triplets.

2610.31938.title: Fidelity Dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings Qubit under Markovian and Non-Markovian Coupling Noise
2610.31938.abstract: We analytically investigate the fidelity dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings qubit coupled to a single-mode cavity in the presence of stochastic fluctuations of the qubit--cavity coupling. Such fluctuations naturally arise in cavity- and circuit-QED platforms due to fabrication imperfections, control-field noise, mechanical vibrations, and environmental disturbances. Since the qubit--cavity coupling governs the rate of coherent energy and information exchange, understanding the effects of its fluctuations is essential for assessing the performance of quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum information-processing protocols. We consider both Gaussian white noise and Ornstein--Uhlenbeck noise with finite correlation time as models for the coupling fluctuations. Exploiting the closed dynamics within each excitation manifold, we derive exact analytical expressions for the noise-averaged density matrix and the fidelity relative to the ideal noiseless evolution. We show that the fidelity is determined by a single decoherence factor governed by the integrated noise correlation function, establishing a direct connection between microscopic coupling fluctuations and macroscopic coherence loss. In the white-noise limit, the fidelity decays exponentially, whereas finite noise correlation times produce nonexponential decay and slower coherence loss. We further show that the crossover between Markovian-like and non-Markovian regimes is controlled by the ratio of the noise correlation rate to the coherent coupling strength, and that decoherence increases with photon number because of the enhanced effective qubit--cavity coupling. These results provide a unified analytical framework for quantifying decoherence induced by stochastic coupling fluctuations and for evaluating the robustness of cavity-QED protocols under correlated noise.
2610.31938.why: Exact fidelity under fluctuating qubit–cavity coupling depends on one decoherence factor set by the integrated noise correlation.

2610.24391.title: Quantum state tomography through multi-frequency Josephson effect
2610.24391.abstract: Macroscopic quantum effects emerge when the coherent behavior of countless microscopic quantum states manifests collectively at a visible scale, as exemplified by the supercurrent carried by innumerable finite-momentum Cooper pairs. By rigorously analyzing the time evolution of superconducting nanodevices including finite-momentum superconductors and quantum-dot Josephson junctions, we analytically derive the ubiquitous macroscopic supercurrent that originates from quantum interference between distinct many-body eigenstates, which we term as the dynamic interference supercurrent. The dynamic interference supercurrent in a system of two Andreev spin qubits exhibits multi-frequency Josephson effect in the absence of external voltage and is governed by the response of the many-body eigenfunctions ($\vert r\rangle$) to variations in the superconducting phase $φ$, determined by the $φ$-space Berry connection $C_{rr'}=\langle r|\partial_φ|r'\rangle$. The macroscopic dynamic interference supercurrent, an inherent property of the superposition state itself, enables an advanced quantum entanglement measurement of the Andreev spin qubits. These findings open new avenues for investigating superconducting nanodevice properties from a wave-function level, with substantial implications for advancing quantum science and technology in solid-state superconducting devices, such as quantum computer, communication, memory, and sensor.
2610.24391.why: Predicts multi-frequency Josephson supercurrents from interference between many-body eigenstates, proposing them as a tomography readout for Andreev spin qubits.

2610.32622.title: Trace-distance characterization of recurrent pairwise synchronization in cavity-coupled superconducting qubits
2610.32622.abstract: We theoretically investigate recurrent pairwise synchronization in three super?conducting qubits coupled to a common single-mode microwave cavity. The qubits interact indirectly through the cavity field and are driven by a coher?ent microwave field. We obtain the coherent dynamics in the dressed-state basis and quantify pairwise synchronization by the trace distance between reduced single-qubit density matrices. The trace-distance dynamics exhibit oscillatory wave-packet structures, with low-trace-distance regions identifying finite syn?chronization windows. An envelope-threshold procedure is introduced to extract the representative duration of these windows. By varying the middle-qubit coupling strength and the relative coupling ratio of the outer qubits, we con?struct a parameter-dependent map of the synchronization-window duration. The duration decreases rapidly with increasing relative outer-qubit coupling and becomes weakly dependent on the middle-qubit coupling in the stronger-coupling regime. These results provide a reduced-state-based characterization of coherent collective dynamics in multiqubit circuit-QED systems.
2610.32622.why: Characterises transient pairwise synchronization of three cavity-coupled driven qubits by trace distance between reduced states.

eli5.plain: A theory study of how three driven qubits sharing one microwave cavity temporarily fall into step with each other.
eli5.how: They solve the dressed-state dynamics and measure how similar two qubits' states are; windows where the difference is small count as synchronization.
eli5.matters: Mostly of conceptual interest: it is a way to describe collective dynamics in a cavity rather than a new optical effect.
eli5.caveat: Coherent dynamics only, an ad hoc threshold defines the windows, and no experimental proposal is given.

2610.26223.title: Sidewall Metrology Protocol for Superconducting Qubit Devices
2610.26223.abstract: Sidewall morphology is a potentially important factor influencing superconducting qubit performance, yet its quantitative characterization remains challenging due to the absence of standardized measurement protocols. In this work, we develop a scanning probe microscopy-based measurement framework for the quantitative characterization of superconducting qubit sidewalls. The framework introduces a refined root mean square lateral sidewall roughness descriptor and a new curvature-equivalent radius for quantifying vertical sidewall morphology. The descriptors and measurement procedures are applied to different components of qubit devices, forming the basis of a proposed sidewall characterization protocol. This provides a foundation for quantitative comparisons of fabrication processes across laboratories, enabling future investigations of correlations between sidewall geometry and qubit performance.
2610.26223.why: Scanning-probe protocol with new roughness and curvature descriptors to quantify qubit sidewall morphology; no link to loss shown.

2610.26892.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
2610.26892.abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the QFT-natural prescription in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem $\,$---$\,$ which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system $\,$---$\,$ is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
2610.26892.why: Argues the soccer-ball problem vanishes for coherent light and proposes a petawatt two-colour delay test of minimal-length physics.

2610.26015.title: Phase engineering of odd parity state in a quantum dot Josephson junction
2610.26015.abstract: Controlling fermion parity in quantum-dot Josephson junctions (QDJJs) enables access to novel superconducting physics. While parity transitions are usually tuned electrically, we study phase-induced transitions in a strongly coupled QDJJ using the superconducting phase difference across the dot terminals, denoted by $φ$. We find that this phase allows control over the ground state parity, with parity transitions observed as the Andreev bound states (ABSs) energies crossing zero. These crossings occur near $φ= π$, and their behavior is in good correspondence to a simple model considering a single-level quantum dot proximitized by a superconductor. These results place phase-controlled QDJJ arrays as a promising platform for exploring exotic phenomena such as Majorana zero modes.
2610.26015.why: Superconducting phase tunes ground-state parity of a strongly coupled quantum-dot Josephson junction, with crossings near π.

2610.29834.title: Teaching quantum mechanics in secondary schools: A qubit-first learning path to Bell's inequalities
2610.29834.abstract: Teaching quantum mechanics at the secondary school level remains a major educational challenge. Traditional historical approaches often present the theory as a sequence of disconnected phenomena, requiring extensive prior knowledge of classical physics before students can appreciate the conceptual structure of quantum physics. In this work, we present the design, implementation, and evaluation of a curriculum based on the two state (qubit first) approach, in which the fundamental postulates of quantum mechanics are introduced through mathematically accessible two level systems and realized with light polarization. The curriculum integrates theoretical instruction, laboratory activities, a coherent progression grounded in the interactive simulations, and inquiry based learning into a coherent pathway that progresses from quantum states and superposition to entanglement and the experimental violation of Bell's inequalities. A distinctive feature of the project is the experimental realization of the violation of Bell's inequalities obtained in a newly established quantum optics laboratory in an Italian high school, where students performed, for the first time in Italy, an authentic Bell test using polarization-entangled photons. The same educational framework was adopted for in service teacher professional development courses. Learning outcomes were evaluated through mixed methods. Preliminary analysis indicates significant improvements in conceptual understanding, confidence in using mathematical formalism, and appreciation of the relationship between theory, experimentation, and the foundations of quantum mechanics. The proposed curriculum shows that two-state formalism and supported by real laboratory experiences enables secondary-school students to engage more meaningfully with both the conceptual foundations of quantum mechanics and their experimental verification.
2610.29834.why: High-school students perform a real polarization-entangled Bell test within a qubit-first curriculum.

eli5.plain: A school curriculum teaches quantum mechanics starting from qubits, ending with students running their own Bell test with entangled photons.
eli5.how: Light polarization stands in for a qubit; lessons, simulations and a school optics lab build up from superposition to entanglement and Bell violation.
eli5.matters: Mainly educational; it shows Bell tests are now a teaching experiment.
eli5.caveat: Learning outcomes are preliminary, and the Bell test itself adds nothing new to foundations.

W7223319095.title: From Macroscopic Quantum Tunneling to Circuit QED: Coherence and Dissipation in 3D Transmon Qubits
W7223319095.abstract: Abstract Superconducting quantum circuits are a leading platform for quantum-information processing, but their development requires expertise spanning device design, microfabrication, cryogenic operation, microwave control, and quantum characterization. In this work, we report the realization of a flux-tunable superconducting transmon platform and present an integrated workflow encompassing design, fabrication, measurement, and numerical modeling. The device consists of an $$Al/AlO_x/Al$$ transmon coupled to a three-dimensional microwave cavity operating in the circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) dispersive regime. Two-tone spectroscopy reveals a fundamental transition frequency of $$\omega _{01}=5.0122~\textrm{GHz}$$ and an anharmonicity of $$\alpha /2\pi =-202.4~\textrm{MHz}$$ , corresponding to $$E_J/E_C \approx 82.9$$ . Flux spectroscopy yields a cavity-qubit coupling strength of $$g/2\pi = 260~\textrm{MHz}$$ , while the cavity linewidth gives a loaded quality factor of $$Q_L=6127$$ and a Purcell limit of $$T_1^{\textrm{Purcell}}\approx 82~\mu \textrm{s}$$ . Time-domain measurements yield coherence times of $$T_1 = 17.4~\mu \textrm{s}$$ and $$T_2^* = 5.8~\mu \textrm{s}$$ . To investigate coherence and dissipation in the device, the experimental observations are analyzed within a Lindblad master-equation framework describing cavity photon loss and thermal excitation, qubit energy relaxation, and pure dephasing processes. Using a set of experimentally extracted parameters, the model reproduces the measured spectroscopic and time-domain observables, providing a quantitative description of the open-system dynamics of the transmon-cavity platform. The analysis shows that the measured coherence is primarily limited by pure dephasing and energy-relaxation processes, whereas thermal excitation plays a minor role under the experimental conditions. Inspired by the broader framework of quantum dissipation in macroscopic quantum systems pioneered by Caldeira and collaborators, this approach enables a quantitative analysis of relaxation and dephasing processes in superconducting quantum circuits. Beyond the characterization of a single device, the present work demonstrates the establishment of the expertise, infrastructure, and experimental workflow required for the design, fabrication, measurement, and modeling of superconducting quantum circuits, contributing to the development of quantum technologies in Brazil and related applications.
W7223319095.why: End-to-end workflow for a flux-tunable 3D transmon in a cavity, from fabrication to modelling; a platform report rather than a new result.

2610.27602.title: Resolving Nonlocal State Reduction via Induced Coherence in Frequency-Comb Biphoton Sources
2610.27602.abstract: How macroscopic definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations emerge from entangled superpositions across spacelike-separated regions without superluminal action or {\it ad hoc} wavefunction collapse remains a defining open question in the foundations of quantum mechanics. Here, we resolve this century-long paradox within \textit{linear} relativistic quantum electrodynamics by developing an open-system and measurement-defined framework realized in dual, spacelike-separated nonlinear crystals driven synchronously by a multi-mode optical frequency comb and seeded by an ultra-narrow coherent laser. Expanding the transverse electromagnetic vector potential into discrete single-photon frequency-comb supermodes, we show that tracing out the unmeasured continuous-wave idler field yields an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation whose decoherence rate is governed by the non-orthogonal state overlap of single-photon-added coherent states. Connecting this open-system map to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory, we demonstrate that single-particle interference arises from the geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than remote collapse, establishing strict operational equivalence across pump, seed, and signal phase scans. The resulting wave-particle-entanglement triality equality $P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$ is saturated across the complete parameter space, while the atomic-clock-referenced comb structure anchors continuous-variable time-frequency displacement stabilizers directly at the hardware layer. Our work unifies induced coherence, Bohr's complementarity, and quotient measurement theory, providing a microscopic pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum information processing.
2610.27602.why: Claims to resolve nonlocal state reduction in linear QED via induced coherence in seeded comb biphoton sources, without engaging existing no-go results.

eli5.plain: The author claims a framework that explains how definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations arise without collapse, using a specific optical setup.

2610.32839.title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
2610.32839.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.
2610.32839.why: Finite temperature destroys quantized transconductance in multiterminal junctions but exposes finite-energy topological Andreev crossings.

W7223056301.title: Scalable quantum circuit for Zeno-enhanced interaction free quantum sensing
W7223056301.abstract: An Elitzur–Vaidman bomb tester demonstrates interaction-free sensing: detecting an object without absorbing a photon. The original protocol, however, has a success probability capped at 25%. We present a scalable quantum circuit that harnesses the quantum Zeno effect to overcome this limit. A single probe qubit undergoes repeated cycles of a small rotation followed by a controlled-NOT (CNOT) with an ancilla qubit representing the obstacle. The circuit requires only two qubits, regardless of the number of cycles N and has depth linear in N, compatible with near-term processors that support mid-circuit measurement and conditional reset. We simulate the circuit under ideal conditions and under a depolarizing noise model with gate errors typical of superconducting qubits (CNOT error 2% and single-qubit gate error rate 0.1%). Under noise, the success probability peaks around N=14 (reaching 72.0%), outperforming the original 25% limit by nearly a factor of three, with a well-defined optimal region. The protocol requires approximately 4.4 times fewer photons than the original Elitzur–Vaidman scheme to achieve 99.9% confidence. Its simple repetitive structure and well-defined optimal regime make it a practical benchmark for quantifying gate errors and decoherence on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware for quantum sensing applications.
W7223056301.why: Two-qubit Zeno circuit beats the 25% Elitzur–Vaidman limit for interaction-free sensing, simulated with noise, not run on hardware.

2610.24891.title: Hidden Perturbative Structure in Attosecond Streaking
2610.24891.abstract: Attosecond streaking is inherently multiphoton, yet we uncover a hidden perturbative structure revealing the underlying continuum--continuum angular-momentum propensity. By filtering the inversion-odd response in helium streaking data at the IR fundamental, we isolate an angular distribution dominated by the $P_1$ and $P_3$ Legendre components, whose complex coefficients yield an effective $s/d$ two-photon amplitude ratio. Multichannel, two-electron time-dependent Schrödinger equation calculations demonstrate that the characteristic Fano propensity survives electron correlation. Incorporating the experimental XUV attochirp reproduces the measured emission-edge trend, while near-threshold calculations predict resonant amplitude and phase signatures associated with the bound He $np$ Rydberg series. This symmetry- and frequency-filtering approach offers a general spectroscopic framework with potential applications to atomic, molecular, and solid-state systems where attosecond streaking is established.
2610.24891.why: Filtering helium streaking data isolates a perturbative two-photon s/d amplitude ratio hidden in the multiphoton signal.

2610.29124.title: Magnetization and Josephson current coupling drives the Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 van der Waals junctions
2610.29124.abstract: The Josephson diode effect (JDE) reflects symmetry breaking in the current-phase relation (CPR) of Josephson junctions, yet establishing its microscopic origin is often challenging. We investigate the mechanism of the JDE in van der Waals Josephson junctions based on FeTe0.55Se0.45, a platform where superconductivity, topology, and magnetism may coexist at the interface. Our devices exhibit a robust zero-field diode response with asymmetric switching currents. Magnetic-field measurements reveal a hysteretic Fraunhofer pattern and magnetic-resonance-induced voltage feature, evidencing interfacial magnetism coupled to the Josephson current. Microwave response further shows half-integer Shapiro steps with asymmetric evolution, demonstrating contributions from both a second harmonic and a magnetization-induced phase shift in CPR. Numerical simulations combining magnetization dynamics and Josephson phase dynamics reproduce these features, confirming that the JDE originates from interfacial coupling between magnetization and Josephson current. This work provides a transport-based route to pinpoint the microscopic mechanism of the JDE, establishing a platform for exploring magnetically active interfacial superconductivity, and enables the design of nonreciprocal superconducting devices in clean, interface-engineered van der Waals systems.
2610.29124.why: Interfacial magnetism coupled to the supercurrent drives the zero-field Josephson diode effect in FeTe0.55Se0.45 junctions.

2610.27856.title: Atmospheric channel model for QKD over satellite megaconstellations
2610.27856.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence and channel loss represent the primary limiting factors in ground-to-satellite quantum communication systems, yet their joint impact remains insufficiently characterized across diverse operational conditions. In this work, we develop a comprehensive and open atmospheric channel model for quantum optical links along ground-to-satellite paths, integrating altitude-dependent molecular and aerosol absorptions. The model is validated with available data from missions such as Micius and Hispasat, including a secondary viability assessment for a hypothetical Starlink-based quantum communication network, where we evaluate the predicted channel behavior in terms of single-photon transmittance and power balance, alongside the channel capacity of the link for uplink and downlink exclusively. Our comparative analysis demonstrates the ability of our channel model to predict real data under simple atmospheric behavior assumptions, which offer practical guidelines for the design and optimization of future quantum satellite missions.
2610.27856.why: Open atmospheric channel model for ground-to-satellite QKD, validated against Micius and Hispasat, applied to a Starlink scenario.

2610.26901.title: Symmetry and Quantum Interference in the Attosecond Domain
2610.26901.abstract: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.
2610.26901.why: Review of symmetry and interference in strong-field photoelectron momentum distributions, with an outlook on non-classical drives.

2610.29021.title: Josephson effect in symmetry-mismatched van der Waals hybrid junctions of NbSe2-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x and NbSe2-Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y
2610.29021.abstract: Coupling superconductors of different symmetries may lead to emergent quantum phenomena but experimental studies on heterojunctions made of lattice-mismatched crystals are scarce. Here, we fabricate Josephson junction by van der Waals stacking NbSe2 flakes on freshly cleaved surfaces of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Bi2Sr2-xLaxCuO6+y. We obtain pronounced Josephson currents across the heterojunctions at temperatures below 7 K. The Josephson coupling strength, characterized by the product of the critical Josephson current I_c and the normal state resistance R_n, can reach about 0.3 mV, much exceeding the values previously reported in Pb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x or Nb-Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x junctions. Microwave irradiation induces integer Shapiro steps. We also observe the Fraunhofer diffraction pattern by applying an in-plane magnetic field. We compare our results with the theoretical calculations that take into account the coherent tunneling and the order parameter mixing. Our work demonstrates the hybrid junctions as a distinctive platform for addressing pairing symmetry and emergent quantum phenomena.
2610.29021.why: NbSe2 stacked on cuprates gives IcRn up to 0.3 mV across symmetry-mismatched van der Waals Josephson junctions.

2610.28453.title: Quantum Simulation of the Static Yukawa Model via Effective Particles on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
2610.28453.abstract: Trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and circuit QED quantum computers naturally enable coupled qubit-boson simulations. Boson-fermion interactions arise in quantum field theory, where renormalization is required to obtain finite results. We study one of the simplest examples of a coupled fermion-boson system, the static Yukawa model, on the QSCOUT trapped-ion system. We use similarity renormalization to express the same physics in terms of effective particles described by different values of the renormalization parameter $s$. This enables us to map data taken in the window of bosonic occupancy that is experimentally accessible to larger occupancies of distinct effective particles. We use this to study strongly coupled, high-occupancy regimes despite limited readout ranges. Using a trapped-ion qubit-boson device on Sandia National Laboratories' QSCOUT platform, we demonstrate the time evolution of the static Yukawa model.
2610.28453.why: Static Yukawa model simulated on the QSCOUT trapped-ion system using similarity renormalization; no superconducting hardware.

2610.32762.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
2610.32762.abstract: Deep learning has transformed radiology, but the computational cost of training and deploying modern models is outpacing what classical hardware can support. Quantum computing has been proposed as one response to this bottleneck: an n-qubit system can represent $2^n$ states simultaneously, although practical speedups require efficient algorithms, data encoding, and measurement strategies rather than superposition alone. This review introduces radiologists to five core quantum concepts, qubits, superposition, entanglement, quantum gates, and quantum circuits, and to the superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic hardware platforms that define the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. We then summarize the quantum machine learning architectures most often applied to medical imaging (quantum support vector machines, quantum neural networks, variational quantum circuits, and quantum convolutional neural networks) and quantum image representations such as the flexible representation of quantum images (FRQI) and the novel enhanced quantum representation (NEQR). Reported applications include brain tumor classification and segmentation on MRI, pneumonia detection on chest radiographs, skin and breast lesion classification, CT and PET reconstruction, and ultrasound denoising. Nearly all published systems are hybrid quantum-classical pipelines evaluated on small, downsampled benchmark datasets or simulators, and clinical deployment is not yet feasible. We conclude with current limitations and translational priorities for radiology.
2610.32762.why: Introductory review of quantum machine learning for radiologists; reported medical results are small-scale simulations.

2610.29779.title: Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (MQE): A Selective State Space Model for Scalable Ground State Simulations in Quantum Chemistry
2610.29779.abstract: Predicting molecular electronic structure using Quantum Computing approaches is a challenge in Computational Chemistry. Traditional Variational Quantum Eigensolvers (VQEs) are typically hindered by optimization challenges. The alternative Generative Quantum Eigensolver (GQE) mitigates this by reformulating ground-state search as discrete sequence generation, but its Transformer backbone suffers from quadratic computational complexity, bottlenecking scalability for larger molecules. To address this, we introduce the Mamba Quantum Eigensolver (Mamba-QE), which replaces the Transformer with a Selective State Space Model (SSM) to process operator sequences with linear $\mathcal{O}(L)$ complexity. Additionally, we integrate a distance-conditioned mechanism enabling the direct prediction of complete potential energy surfaces (PES). Evaluated on the $H_2$ molecule, Mamba-QE reproduces Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) reference energies well within chemical accuracy, achieving an energy error below $3\times10^{-6}$ Ha across 16 geometries with zero variational violations. Mamba-QE maintains high expressive power while establishing a robust, scalable foundation for quantum simulations of complex molecular systems.
2610.29779.why: Swaps the Transformer in a generative eigensolver for a Mamba state-space model, tested only on H2.
